intro.text: Hi, I'm the narrator. I'm an AI voice running on Mike's Mac Studio, which means I live in his basement, same as this website. Mike spent thirteen years keeping a carrier network running, and he has a deep personal grudge against doing anything twice. Scroll at your own pace. I'll keep up.

tldr.text: The short version. Thirteen years as a network engineer at Charter. Python automation since 2020. Two years on a dev-ops team. And now, AI tools, built and run on his own hardware.

thesis.text: Mike has one rule. Do it once by hand. Do it twice and complain about it. The third time, a computer does it. The tools keep changing. The rule doesn't.

story.text: Here's the route. Tech school, then Charter in 2013, turning up fiber circuits by the thousand. A spreadsheet that turned an hour of work into five minutes. Python. A dev-ops team. And in June 2026, a very busy week: a new baby on Tuesday, and a closed office on Friday.

numbers.text: A few numbers worth knowing. Up to two thousand circuits a year, by himself. A region-wide rollout he automated solo, while other regions used five or six engineers. And when he moved to the dev-ops team, it took six people to cover his old job.

lab.text: This is the lab in his basement. A control room for all his AI, a house voice named Thaddeus who reads tornado warnings at three in the morning, monitoring that makes failures loud, and a garden planner called GrowYear. His family uses all of it. Some of them even like it.

before.text: None of this started with AI. Mike was wiring up garage doors, plant waterers and pepper sensors years before a computer could help him write the code. AI just made him faster.

garden.text: A gardener who starts young gets about sixty gardens in a lifetime. That's why Mike builds tools. So the computers get more of the chores, and his family gets more of him.

built.text: Everything you're seeing and hearing was made by AI models running on Mike's own Mac Studio. And the page itself is coming to you from a Raspberry Pi in his basement, through a tunnel over satellite internet. Including me. Hi again.

how.text: How he works. Do it twice, then script it. Be the first one in. Make failures loud. And let the AI ask before it does anything that matters.

next.text: What he's after: a small team that wants the boring stuff gone. Anywhere from Madison to Milwaukee, hybrid if he can get it.

contact.text: That's the tour. If any of this sounds like your team, his email is right there. Okay, cool. Thanks for listening.
